title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sits inside Grothendieck's c.1970 attempt to describe an object G (most plausibly an abelian variety or 1-motive type object, or a p-divisible/Barsotti–Tate datum over Z) by a 'system of realizations'. The pair (M,T) is a rational structure M with extra data T. It is glued to local or adelic realizations: t_{A'} = (T_{A'}, u_{A'}) for the finite-adelic (Tate-module) part away from p, t_∞ at the archimedean place, and t_p at p (crystalline/Dieudonné, cf. the F–V triangles of the neighbouring pages). The working hypothesis is that the relevant automorphism group is μ2 = {±1}.

Section 3 (indeterminacy of the local data for fixed (M,T), i.e. fixed G). The category E_B of possible completions is a torsor under the Picard groupoid of μ2-torsors over the adeles. So its isomorphism classes form a torsor under H^1(A^f, μ2). This group is the restricted product of the Q_p^*/Q_p^{*2}, with almost all components in Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2}. The automorphism group of any object is H^0(A', μ2) = ∏_p Z/2.

Section 4 (rigidity). Fix (M',T') isomorphic to (M,T) up to the stated equivalence. The category of equivalences (M,T,t_{A'},t_∞,t_p) → (M',T',...) is either empty or a torsor under the groupoid of μ2-torsors over Q trivialized over A. Its π0 is the relative cohomology H^1(Q mod A, μ2), which sits in the exact sequence
μ2(Q) → μ2(A) → H^1(Q mod A, μ2) → H^1(Q, μ2) = Q^*/Q^{*2} → H^1(A, μ2).
- Squares satisfy the Hasse principle (a rational number that is a square everywhere locally is a square), so the last map is injective.
- Hence H^1(Q mod A, μ2) = (∏_v Z/2)/(±1). This is identified with the 2-torsion ₂(J_Q) of the idèle class group: x^2 = q ∈ Q^* forces q = r^2, and then x/r ∈ ∏{±1}. It has the cardinality of the continuum.
- H^0(Q mod A, μ2) = ker(μ2(Q) → μ2(A)) = 0, so the category is rigid.
- Since H^1(Q mod A) maps to zero in H^1(Q, μ2), the induced equivalence between (M,T) and (M',T') is determined up to unique isomorphism.

Conclusion: one may harmlessly identify (M,T) with (M',T'). This is a 'gerbe/torsor of gluings' argument showing that the global rational object is canonically determined by its local or adelic realizations, despite a huge (continuum) set of non-isomorphic gluing data.
errors: Grothendieck writes a coproduct ∐_p Q_p^*/Q_p^{*2}. The correct object is the restricted product (components in Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} for almost all p), which his own marginal gloss indicates.
∏_p Z/2Z should include the archimedean place if A denotes the full adeles (A versus A'/A^f notation is not used consistently). This does not affect the argument.

The identification of H^1(Q mod A, μ2) with ₂(J_Q) is correct only with J_Q read as the idèle class group A^*/Q^*, and it depends on the Hasse principle for squares (no Grunwald–Wang obstruction for μ2 over Q). This is fine here but not stated.

ideas.what: Classifying ambiguity in gluing data (rational structure plus adelic/local realizations) as a torsor under the Picard groupoid of μ2-torsors over the adeles, with π0 = H^1(A, μ2) and π1 = H^0(A, μ2)
ideas.modern_name: Torsor under a Picard stack / gerbe-theoretic description of gluing of realizations (adelic double-coset descriptions of isogeny or isomorphism classes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Adelic double-coset descriptions: Weil, Shimura, Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971, Variétés de Shimura 1979). Torsor/gerbe formalism: Giraud 1971.
ideas.where_published: Torsors under Picard categories appear in SGA4 XVIII (Deligne) and Giraud; this specific adelic application is not known in Grothendieck's published texts

ideas.what: Relative cohomology H^i(Q mod A, μ2) and its computation via the Hasse principle: H^0 = 0, H^1 = (∏_v Z/2)/±1 = ₂(idèle class group), with zero image in H^1(Q, μ2)
ideas.modern_name: Relative Galois/étale cohomology of Q with respect to adeles; Tate–Shafarevich-type kernels (Ш^1(Q, μ2) = 0)

ideas.what: Rigidity: a global rational object is determined up to unique isomorphism by compatible local realizations (ℓ-adic, archimedean, crystalline at p)
ideas.modern_name: Systems of realizations (Deligne, Jannsen); full faithfulness of realization functors
ideas.where_published: Motivic ideas are described in Récoltes et Semailles; no published technical treatment by Grothendieck

missed.claim: In c.1970, within the crystalline project, Grothendieck treats the comparison data between a rational structure and its adelic plus crystalline realizations as a torsor under the Picard groupoid of μ2-torsors on A. He uses the relative cohomology H^*(Q mod A, μ2) and the Hasse principle to prove the gluing is unique up to unique isomorphism. This is an early, explicitly stack-theoretic formulation of 'objects over Z/Q = rational structure + adelic realizations + crystalline data at p'. It anticipates both systems of realizations and the adelic-uniformization style of argument.
missed.quote: Comme l'image de H^1(Q mod A, μ2) dans H^1(Q, μ2) est nulle, on voit que l'équivalence induite entre (M,T) et (M',T') est déterminée à isom. unique près.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck combining crystalline (F–V) data at p with adelic data via torsor/gerbe language around 1970. The mathematics itself is routine to a modern specialist.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is elementary (Hasse principle for squares). The interesting part is historical: an early gerbe-style treatment of gluing adelic, archimedean and crystalline realizations into a rigid global object, next to the crystalline Dieudonné-theory F–V triangle notes. It is not a new result for specialists today.
transcription_corrections: '∐_p Q_p^*/Q_p^{*2}' is a restricted product. The marginal gloss reads roughly '(i.e. à composantes dans Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} sauf pour un nombre fini)' rather than 'dans tous sauf val. à l'un des'.
'H^1(Q mod A, μ2)': the superscript 1 is overwritten on another symbol in the manuscript.
'₂(J_Q)' means the 2-torsion of the idèle class group J_Q.
The interlinear insertion above 'données' in §4 reads like '≃ mod.' or '≃ iso'; it is uncertain.
The left margin note ('modulo une ligne venant... mod 2, comme l'a...') is largely illegible; the transcription there is unreliable.
